draft.title: Rock types and landforms
card: rock that forms when melted rock, called magma, cools and sets hard. Granite and basalt are examples.
rock that forms when layers of sediment (pieces of rock, sand, mud or shell) are pressed and cemented together. Sandstone and limestone are examples.
rock that forms when existing rock is changed by heat and pressure, without melting. Marble and slate are examples.
Rocks differ in hardness. Harder rock resists erosion and is left standing as hills or ridges. Softer rock wears away faster and forms lower ground.
draft.remember: Rock type depends on how the rock formed. Harder rock wears away slowly, so it stands out.

a.q: Sandstone is made of sand grains pressed and cemented in layers. What type of rock is it?
a.why: Rock made of pressed and cemented layers of sediment is sedimentary. Igneous rock is tempting because it is common in landforms, but it forms from cooled magma, not from layers of grains.
a.clue: Think about how the rock was built up.

b.q: A hard granite ridge rises above a plain of softer mudstone in Western Australia. Why does the ridge stand higher?
opts: The granite wore away more slowly than the mudstone
The granite was pushed up after the mudstone wore down
The mudstone is igneous and the granite is sedimentary
The mudstone is harder, so it was buried by sediment
b.why: Hard rock resists erosion, so it is left standing while softer rock around it wears away. The idea that the granite was pushed up later is tempting, but the card says the height comes from different rates of erosion.
b.clue: Which rock is lost faster when wind and water wear it?

b.best: The granite wore away more slowly than the mudstone
